chapters.title: Your Canadian certificate
chapters.summary: Understand the qualification you are working toward, the exam, and the responsibilities that come with a call sign.
objectives: Explain Basic and Basic with Honours

lessons.title: Who makes the rules?
lessons.teachingSummary: Canada's Radiocommunication Act is the enabling law: it gives the federal government authority to regulate radiocommunications and publish operating standards. Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) administers it. The Radiocommunication Regulations give more detailed legal requirements and define the amateur radio service. RBR-4 contains the operating standards, including bands, bandwidths and power restrictions.
lessons.teaching:
Canada's Radiocommunication Act is the enabling law: it gives the federal government authority to regulate radiocommunications and publish operating standards. Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) administers it. The Radiocommunication Regulations give more detailed legal requirements and define the amateur radio service. RBR-4 contains the operating standards, including bands, bandwidths and power restrictions.

Think of three layers: the Act gives authority; the Regulations implement requirements; the standards supply operating details. The Broadcasting Act concerns broadcasting and is not the enabling law for amateur radio. The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) coordinates internationally; it does not replace Canada's domestic legislation.

Worked distinction: a question asking which document gives authority points to the Act. A question asking which document defines the Canadian amateur radio service points to the Regulations. A question asking which department administers the Act points to ISED.

ISED B-001-001-001

Which document assigns the authority to make Canadian regulations governing radiocommunications?

Correct answer: The Radiocommunication Act

ISED B-001-001-002

Which document assigns the authority to publish Standards for the Operation of Radio Stations in the Amateur Radio Service in Canada?

Correct answer: The Radiocommunication Act

ISED B-001-001-003

Which department is responsible for the administration of the Radiocommunication Act?

Correct answer: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

ISED B-001-001-004

Which document defines the Canadian "amateur radio service"?

Correct answer: The Radiocommunication Regulations

lessons.title: Your certificate, address changes and fees
lessons.teachingSummary: An Amateur Radio Operator Certificate is valid for life. There is no annual certificate renewal. Keep the certificate at the station/address supplied to ISED, and update ISED within 30 days after your mailing address changes. If an inspector requests your certificate or a copy, the examination bank allows 48 hours to produce it. Lifetime validity does not remove these administrative duties.

Keep the certificate at the station/address supplied to ISED, and update ISED within 30 days after your mailing address changes. If an inspector requests your certificate or a copy, the examination bank allows 48 hours to produce it. Lifetime validity does not remove these administrative duties.

ServiceFee in the official bank
First certificate and initial call signFree
Replacement prefix after moving to another province or territoryFree
Changing an existing call sign, including a two-letter call sign$60

Example: moving from Ontario to another province can require an address/prefix update; notifying ISED is still due within 30 days even though the qualifying replacement is free. Choosing a different existing call sign for preference is a different service and has the $60 fee. Fees and procedures should be checked with ISED before an actual application.

ISED B-001-002-001

What must you do within 30 days of a mailing address change?

Correct answer: Inform Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

ISED B-001-002-002

An Amateur Radio Operator Certificate is valid for:

Correct answer: life

ISED B-001-002-003

Whenever a change of address is made:

Correct answer: you must notify Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada within 30 days of a change of mailing address

ISED B-001-002-004

The Amateur Radio Operator Certificate:

Correct answer: must be retained at the station

ISED B-001-002-005

A radio inspector asks to see your Amateur Radio Operator Certificate, or a copy thereof. Per the regulations, how many hours are you given to comply?

Correct answer: 48

ISED B-001-002-006

What is the fee for a first Amateur Radio Operator Certificate?

Correct answer: Free

ISED B-001-002-007

The Amateur Radio Operator Certificate should be:

Correct answer: retained at the address provided to Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada

ISED B-001-002-008

What is the fee to issue a replacement call sign with a new prefix, due to a change in address to a new province or territory?

Correct answer: Free

ISED B-001-002-009

What is the fee for changing an existing call sign (including changing to a two-letter call sign)?

Correct answer: $60

lessons.title: Offences, inspections and fair process
lessons.teachingSummary: Your certificate authorizes operation only within its privileges. Deliberate obstruction, false information and a false distress call are prohibited. Calling MAYDAY when there is no distress is a false or fraudulent message. The official bank asks for a maximum $5,000 fine, one year of imprisonment, or both, for the stated individual false-distress/interference offences. Do not confuse a question's specified offence with every possible penalty under the Act.
lessons.teaching:
Your certificate authorizes operation only within its privileges. Deliberate obstruction, false information and a false distress call are prohibited. Calling MAYDAY when there is no distress is a false or fraudulent message. The official bank asks for a maximum $5,000 fine, one year of imprisonment, or both, for the stated individual false-distress/interference offences. Do not confuse a question's specified offence with every possible penalty under the Act.

The Minister can suspend a certificate for contraventions, misrepresentation or unpaid required fees, subject to applicable notice and opportunity to make representations. The claim that suspension can simply occur with neither notice nor an opportunity to respond is the incorrect selection in the bank's NOT-correct question.

An inspector does not have an unrestricted right to enter a dwelling without consent and without a warrant. A warrant may authorize necessary entry, and using force requires the specified authorization and peace-officer involvement. Read NOT questions carefully: the selected answer can be the false statement, rather than a rule you should follow.

ISED B-001-003-001

Transmissions outside of amateur radio bands:

Correct answer: are prohibited and penalties could be assessed to the control operator

ISED B-001-003-002

What is the term in the regulations that defines if an amateur radio operator falsely transmits the word "MAYDAY" when there isn't an emergency?

Correct answer: A false or fraudulent message

ISED B-001-003-003

Transmitting a false or fraudulent distress signal or message is prohibited. The person found guilty is liable to what penalty?

Correct answer: A fine, not exceeding $5 000, or a prison term not exceeding one year, or both

ISED B-001-003-004

Which government document states the offences and penalties relating to radiocommunications?

Correct answer: The Radiocommunication Act

ISED B-001-003-005

Which of the following is NOT correct? The Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry may suspend an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate:

False statement to select: with no notice, or opportunity to make representations thereto

Select this because it is the false statement. Suspension is subject to the applicable notice and opportunity to make representations; do not memorize the selected wording as an unrestricted ministerial power.

ISED B-001-003-006

Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

False statement to select: A radio inspector may enter a dwelling without the consent of the occupant and without a warrant

Select this because it is false: an inspector does not have a general power to enter a dwelling with neither consent nor a warrant. The other choices describe conditions associated with authorized inspection.

ISED B-001-003-007

When is an amateur radio operator permitted to transmit false information?

Correct answer: Transmitting false information is never permitted

ISED B-001-003-008

Interfering with, or obstructing any radio communication, without lawful cause, is prohibited. The person found guilty is liable to what penalty?

Correct answer: A fine, not exceeding $5 000, or a prison term not exceeding one year, or both

lessons.title: Qualifying and adding endorsements
lessons.teachingSummary: There is no minimum or maximum age for Basic certification. Candidates need a valid address in Canada, and Basic is the entry examination before an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate is issued. Some specified existing Canadian radio qualifications, such as the Radiocommunication Operator General Certificate Maritime (RGMC), can support the certificate arrangements described by ISED.
lessons.teaching:
There is no minimum or maximum age for Basic certification. Candidates need a valid address in Canada, and Basic is the entry examination before an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate is issued. Some specified existing Canadian radio qualifications, such as the Radiocommunication Operator General Certificate Maritime (RGMC), can support the certificate arrangements described by ISED.

After Basic you may pursue the Advanced and Morse qualifications in either order. The separate Morse endorsement uses 5 words per minute sending and receiving. You do not need that endorsement merely to use Morse on bands already authorized by your qualifications.

Advanced is an amateur radio qualification. It does not itself grant aviation, marine or land-mobile operating authority. A certificate's amateur privileges and a different service's equipment/operator requirements are separate matters.

ISED B-001-004-001

How old must you be to hold an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate with Basic Qualification?

Correct answer: There are no age limits

ISED B-001-004-002

Which examination must be passed before an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate is issued?

Correct answer: Basic Qualification

ISED B-001-004-003

Holders of which one of the following certificates may be issued an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate?

Correct answer: Canadian Radiocommunication Operator General Certificate Maritime (RGMC)

ISED B-001-004-004

After an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate with Basic Qualification is issued, the holder may be examined for additional qualifications in the following order:

Correct answer: any order

ISED B-001-004-005

Correct answer: 5 wpm

Correct answer: No other service

What conditions must candidates for amateur radio certification meet?

Correct answer: Have a valid address in Canada

lessons.title: Installing or repairing a station for someone else
lessons.teachingSummary: An amateur authorization is not permission to install transmitting equipment for an unqualified customer or friend. For installing, placing in service or repairing an amateur transmitter on another person's behalf, both you and that person must hold Amateur Radio Operator Certificates with the qualifications required for the activity.
lessons.teaching:
An amateur authorization is not permission to install transmitting equipment for an unqualified customer or friend. For installing, placing in service or repairing an amateur transmitter on another person's behalf, both you and that person must hold Amateur Radio Operator Certificates with the qualifications required for the activity.

The owner needs the appropriate authorization for the apparatus. An Advanced-qualified amateur working on equipment for someone else does not substitute their own certificate for the other person's authorization. Reprogramming a land-mobile transmitter for someone else's use on 2 metres requires that other person to hold amateur certification, as well as compliance with the applicable amateur apparatus rules.

Distinguish helping a qualified station owner from letting an unqualified person transmit while supervised. The latter is a separate operating situation taught in the control-operator lesson.

Under what circumstances can an amateur radio operator with an Advanced Qualification install, place in operation, modify or repair radio apparatus on behalf of another person?

Under what circumstances can an amateur radio operator reprogram a land mobile transmitter on behalf of another person for use on 2 metres?

lessons.title: Amateur authority and equipment certification
lessons.teachingSummary: Even a 2-watt amateur transmitter requires supervision by a qualified amateur with a call sign. Low power alone does not make amateur operation licence-exempt. Amateur stations normally communicate with stations under similar authorizations; amateur certification does not confer a general entitlement to use marine, aeronautical or land-mobile channels.
lessons.teaching:
Even a 2-watt amateur transmitter requires supervision by a qualified amateur with a call sign. Low power alone does not make amateur operation licence-exempt. Amateur stations normally communicate with stations under similar authorizations; amateur certification does not confer a general entitlement to use marine, aeronautical or land-mobile channels.

Frequency capability is not permission. A radio programmed onto a commercial channel must meet the certification and licensing requirements of that service. An amateur radio that can tune there is not automatically certified there. Conversely, equipment originally made for another service may be usable within amateur bands when the appropriate amateur conditions are met.

Do not add an amplifier to a licence-exempt transmitter under the assumption that an amateur certificate authorizes it. The licence-exempt device has its own equipment and emission conditions. For ordinary operation, use the bands and equipment authorization applicable to the service you are actually using.

ISED B-001-006-001

An amateur radio station with a maximum power output of 2 watts:

Correct answer: must be under the supervision of a person holding an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate and call sign

ISED B-001-006-002

An amateur radio station may be used to communicate with:

Correct answer: stations operated under similar authorizations

ISED B-001-006-003

Under what circumstances is an amateur radio operator permitted to use an amplifier to amplify the output of a licence-exempt transmitter?

Correct answer: This is not permitted

ISED B-001-006-004

When is it permissible to use amateur radio equipment, with or without modification, to transmit outside amateur radio bands?

Correct answer: Never, amateur radio equipment is not certified for operation outside amateur radio bands

ISED B-001-006-005

Which of the following statements is NOT correct? A person may operate radio apparatus, authorized in the amateur radio service:

False statement to select: on aeronautical, marine or land mobile frequencies

This is the false statement. Amateur authority alone does not authorize aeronautical, marine or land-mobile operation. A separate service has its own licensing, certification and operator conditions.

ISED B-001-006-006

Some VHF and UHF FM radios purchased for use in the amateur radio service can also be programmed to communicate on frequencies used for the land mobile service. Under what conditions is this permissible?

Correct answer: The radio is certified and licensed for use in the land mobile service

lessons.title: Basic versus Advanced station privileges
lessons.teachingSummary: Basic permits operating amateur stations anywhere in Canada within the holder's privileges, assembling professionally designed commercially available transmitter kits, and operating cross-band repeaters. These are different activities from installing a same-band voice repeater or establishing a club station.
lessons.teaching:
Basic permits operating amateur stations anywhere in Canada within the holder's privileges, assembling professionally designed commercially available transmitter kits, and operating cross-band repeaters. These are different activities from installing a same-band voice repeater or establishing a club station.

Basic plus Advanced is required for the bank's examples of installing a same-band voice repeater, installing an amateur club station, using transmitting equipment or an RF amplifier that is neither professionally designed nor commercially manufactured for amateur use, and remotely controlling frequency, mode or power.

A beacon is an example of permitted one-way amateur communication. A general-public broadcast is not made permissible merely by calling it a beacon. Operating an existing repeater is also different from being qualified to install it.

Memory aid: read the verb in the question—operate, assemble, install, design and remotely control can have different qualification requirements.

Where may holders of an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate operate an amateur radio station in Canada?

Correct answer: Anywhere in Canada

ISED B-001-008-002

Which type of station may transmit one-way communications?

Correct answer: Beacon station

ISED B-001-008-003

What minimum qualifications must an amateur radio operator hold to assemble commercially available transmitter kits of professional design?

Correct answer: Basic

ISED B-001-008-004

What minimum qualifications must an amateur radio operator hold to install a repeater operating on a single band in a voice mode?

Correct answer: Basic and Advanced

ISED B-001-008-005

ISED B-001-008-006

ISED B-001-008-007

What minimum qualifications must an amateur radio operator hold to operate cross-band repeaters?

Correct answer: Basic

ISED B-001-008-008

What minimum qualifications must an amateur radio operator hold to remotely operate a transmitter, including changing frequency, emission mode or output power?

Correct answer: Basic and Advanced

lessons.title: Bands and the privileges of visiting operators
lessons.teachingSummary: The privileges used at a station cannot exceed either the station authorization being used or the control operator's own qualifications. Inviting an Advanced operator to use your more restricted station/call sign does not automatically upgrade its privileges. An operator with fewer qualifications at an Advanced station cannot use privileges they personally lack.
lessons.teaching:
The privileges used at a station cannot exceed either the station authorization being used or the control operator's own qualifications. Inviting an Advanced operator to use your more restricted station/call sign does not automatically upgrade its privileges. An operator with fewer qualifications at an Advanced station cannot use privileges they personally lack.

For access below 30 MHz, the usual current routes are Basic with Honours (80% or better), Basic plus Advanced, or Basic plus the Morse qualification. Basic passes at 70%. Radio control of models uses amateur bands above 30 MHz. A separate repeater-output exception is covered in the repeater-rules lesson.

Band nameCanadian frequency range asked in the bank
160 metres1.8–2.0 MHz
80 metres3.5–4.0 MHz
40 metres7.0–7.3 MHz
20 metres14.000–14.350 MHz
15 metres21.000–21.450 MHz
10 metres28.000–29.700 MHz

These are allocation edges, not guarantees that every mode fits at every frequency. The entire occupied signal must remain inside the band and satisfy its bandwidth and power limits.

If you let another amateur radio operator with additional qualifications than yours control your station and operate under your call sign, what operating privileges are allowed?

If you are the control operator at the station of another amateur radio operator who has more certificate qualifications than you, what operating privileges are you allowed?

In addition to passing the Basic written examination, what must you do before you are allowed to use amateur radio frequencies below 30 MHz?

The holder of an Amateur Radio Operator Certificate may operate radio-controlled models:

What is the frequency range of the 80-metre amateur radio band in Canada?

ISED B-001-015-006

What is the frequency range of the 160-metre amateur radio band in Canada?

Correct answer: 1.8 MHz to 2.0 MHz

ISED B-001-015-007

What is the frequency range of the 40-metre amateur radio band in Canada?

Correct answer: 7.0 MHz to 7.3 MHz

ISED B-001-015-008

What is the frequency range of the 20-metre amateur radio band in Canada?

Correct answer: 14.000 MHz to 14.350 MHz

ISED B-001-015-009

What is the frequency range of the 15-metre amateur radio band in Canada?

Correct answer: 21.000 MHz to 21.450 MHz

What is the frequency range of the 10-metre amateur radio band in Canada?

lessons.title: Occupied bandwidth and band edges
lessons.teachingSummary: Bandwidth is the span occupied by a transmission, not its centre frequency. Keep the complete signal inside the permitted band. Selecting a dial frequency just inside an edge is insufficient if a sideband extends beyond it.
lessons.teaching:
Bandwidth is the span occupied by a transmission, not its centre frequency. Keep the complete signal inside the permitted band. Selecting a dial frequency just inside an edge is insufficient if a sideband extends beyond it.

Band or range in the examMaximum occupied bandwidth
7–25 MHz bands, except 30 metres6 kHz
30 metres: 10.100–10.150 MHz1 kHz
10 metres: 28.000–29.700 MHz20 kHz
6 metres: 50–54 MHz30 kHz
2 metres: 144–148 MHz30 kHz

Ordinary SSB voice is about 2–3 kHz wide, so it does not fit the 30-metre 1-kHz limit: SSB at 10.12 MHz is prohibited. Fast-scan television is much wider than the allowed limits on 2 metres and 20 metres, so the bank's ATV examples at 145 MHz and 14.23 MHz are prohibited.

Worked band-edge example: an LSB signal with audio extending to 3 kHz is transmitted below its suppressed-carrier frequency. At a lower band edge, allow that occupied width above the edge in your dial setting. USB extends above its suppressed-carrier setting instead.

lessons.title: Power limits: read the measurement being asked
lessons.teachingSummary: Use the minimum legal power needed for communication. DC input power, carrier/RF output, peak envelope power (PEP), ERP and EIRP measure different things and cannot be substituted for one another. PEP is the RF-cycle-average power at the crest of the modulation envelope.
lessons.teaching:
Use the minimum legal power needed for communication. DC input power, carrier/RF output, peak envelope power (PEP), ERP and EIRP measure different things and cannot be substituted for one another. PEP is the RF-cycle-average power at the crest of the modulation envelope.

QualificationFinal-stage DC inputNon-SSB carrier outputSSB PEP output
Without Advanced250 W190 W560 W
With Advanced1000 W750 W2250 W

For example, Basic with Honours and Basic plus Morse have HF access, but neither alone supplies Advanced power privileges: the bank's SSB examples at 7055 kHz and 3750 kHz use a 560-W PEP limit. The 250-W figure is DC input to the final amplifier, not 250 W of RF output.

Special-band radiated-power limits can be lower: the bank asks for 100 W ERP as PEP on 60 metres, even with Advanced. On 630 and 2200 metres, limits are expressed as EIRP, so antenna gain must be included. Verify allowed transmitter/amplifier output at that device's output connector after accounting for exposure and radiated-power restrictions. A general maximum never overrides a stricter band-specific or RF-exposure limit.

lessons.title: International amateur communications
lessons.teachingSummary: International amateur contacts are for amateur-service purposes and personal remarks, not commercial traffic. They are generally allowed unless an administration has registered an objection. The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) publishes international Radio Regulations; Canada implements its own national requirements within that framework.
lessons.teaching:

The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) publishes international Radio Regulations; Canada implements its own national requirements within that framework.

An international regulation does not require every country to impose the same Morse test. Administrations decide whether Morse proficiency is required for their authorizations. Canada's Basic, Honours, Advanced and Morse arrangements must therefore be learned as Canadian rules rather than inferred from another country's licence classes.

For an international contact, ask two questions: is communication with that administration allowed, and does the proposed content fit amateur purposes/personal remarks? Third-party traffic has its own additional conditions and is covered with operating procedures.

lessons.title: ITU regions and operating abroad
lessons.teachingSummary: The ITU divides the world into three radio regions. Region 1 includes Europe and Africa; Region 2 includes Canada and the Americas; Region 3 includes Australia, Japan and Southeast Asia. Allocations can differ by region and country.

When visiting another country, obey that country's frequency limits and the privileges allowed by the applicable agreement. A Canadian station in Florida, including the bank's example 7 km offshore, uses the US band limits. Basic is the minimum Canadian qualification asked for visiting operation in the United States. For the CEPT Amateur Radio Licence arrangement in the bank, the Canadian minimum is Advanced. In a participating country, identify with that country's prefix, then stroke, then your Canadian call sign. CEPT and the Canada–US arrangements are not identical: check current permit documents and operating conditions before travelling.

lessons.title: Exam administration and accommodations
lessons.teachingSummary: ISED office qualification examinations have no examination fee. An accredited examiner may recover the costs of administering an exam; that is distinct from a fee for issuing the first certificate. An accredited examiner must hold Basic, Advanced and Morse qualifications under the criteria used in this bank.

An accredited examiner must hold Basic, Advanced and Morse qualifications under the criteria used in this bank.

Accommodations change how a candidate demonstrates knowledge; they do not excuse portions of the required knowledge. Examples include an oral examination for appropriate reading/language difficulties and an adapted Morse sending method. Medical evidence may be requested for an accommodation. An interpreter is not the bank's permitted substitute for demonstrating the required English/French examination knowledge.

Three NOT-correct traps select false claims: a $5-per-qualification ISED-office fee; exemption from parts of the examination due to disability; and bringing an interpreter as described in the question. Do not memorize those claims as true rules. Discuss an appropriate accommodation with the examiner before booking.

lessons.title: The control operator and shared responsibility
lessons.teachingSummary: Both the station owner and the control operator are responsible for lawful station operation. A qualified owner may choose another appropriately qualified amateur as control operator. A control operator is required whenever the station transmits and must be at its control point.
lessons.teaching:
Both the station owner and the control operator are responsible for lawful station operation. A qualified owner may choose another appropriately qualified amateur as control operator. A control operator is required whenever the station transmits and must be at its control point.

An unqualified friend or family member may speak through your station only under the supervision and in the presence of someone holding the appropriate qualifications. Leaving equipment available at home does not authorize an unqualified person to be the control operator when alone.

Worked situation: a visiting friend speaks on your microphone while you remain present, monitor the conversation and control the transmitter. That is supervised operation. Giving them your call sign and leaving is not equivalent. Visiting operators and station qualifications can also limit which bands and powers may be used.

lessons.title: Distress exceptions and disaster relief
lessons.teachingSummary: Ordinary amateur contacts are with other amateur stations. Do not turn the existence of a disaster into general permission to use out-of-band channels. The bank explicitly distinguishes routine relief operations after a disaster from an immediate distress situation involving safety of life or property.
lessons.teaching:
Ordinary amateur contacts are with other amateur stations. Do not turn the existence of a disaster into general permission to use out-of-band channels. The bank explicitly distinguishes routine relief operations after a disaster from an immediate distress situation involving safety of life or property.

A station actually in distress may use any means of radiocommunication, and the distress question does not impose ordinary transmitter-power limits. If you hear an unanswered distress call on an amateur band where you normally lack privileges, the bank allows you to respond and offer assistance. These narrow distress provisions are not a general operating exemption.

Disaster-relief communications are appropriate when ordinary systems are damaged, disrupted or overloaded. Operators not directly involved should avoid needless transmissions near the relief-net frequency. Messages for recognized public-service agencies can be handled in peacetime exercises as well as emergencies. Distress-related necessary intervention is different from deliberate interference with ordinary contacts.

lessons.title: No payment and the privacy of intercepted communications
lessons.teachingSummary: Do not demand or accept payment for handling amateur or third-party messages. The service is not a paid message-delivery business. A friendly request and a third-party message do not create an exception for remuneration.
lessons.teaching:
Do not demand or accept payment for handling amateur or third-party messages. The service is not a paid message-delivery business. A friendly request and a third-party message do not create an exception for remuneration.

Amateur transmissions are among the communications that may be divulged or used under the applicable rules. Do not extend that to every radio signal you can receive. Non-broadcast, non-amateur communications can remain protected even when audible with ordinary receiving equipment. Supplying intercepted protected content to answer a media organization's questions is an offence in the example asked.

Separate the right to receive a signal from the right to disclose or use its contents. The fact that a receiver or SDR can tune a frequency does not itself settle the disclosure question.

lessons.title: Call signs and identification intervals
lessons.teachingSummary: Identify your amateur station by transmitting its assigned call sign at the beginning and end of each contact and at intervals no longer than 30 minutes. Each station identifies itself. The same identification requirements apply to test transmissions; saying testing instead of a call sign is insufficient.
lessons.teaching:
Identify your amateur station by transmitting its assigned call sign at the beginning and end of each contact and at intervals no longer than 30 minutes. Each station identifies itself. The same identification requirements apply to test transmissions; saying testing instead of a call sign is insufficient.

Identification may be in English or French. Normal Canadian amateur prefixes include VA, VE, VO and VY; VA3RAC is a valid-format example in the bank. Phonetics clarify the letters but do not replace the assigned call sign.

The exception asked for unidentified operation is controlling a model craft. Do not apply that exception to conversation or to equipment testing. Example: for a 45-minute contact, identify at the start, again before the first 30 minutes elapse, and at its end.

lessons.title: Third parties and foreign visitors in Canada
lessons.teachingSummary: A third party is someone on whose behalf an amateur communicates, including a supervised person without amateur certification. Both non-certified friends at the two ends are third parties. Third-party content must remain personal and non-commercial, and the certified operators remain responsible.
lessons.teaching:
A third party is someone on whose behalf an amateur communicates, including a supervised person without amateur certification. Both non-certified friends at the two ends are third parties. Third-party content must remain personal and non-commercial, and the certified operators remain responsible.

Canada does not prohibit international third-party amateur communications. Check the foreign administration's conditions; emergency/disaster-relief third-party communications are expressly permitted unless that administration specifically prohibits them. If a foreign amateur joins while your unqualified friend is speaking, remain present and continue monitoring; do not abandon supervision.

Foreign visitors need the applicable reciprocal authority or permit. CEPT visitors receive Canadian privileges equivalent to Advanced, subject to the conditions of their own authorization. A US visitor operating by voice in Canada uses their US call sign with mobile/portable as appropriate and the Canadian geographic prefix, and supplies city and province at least once during the contact. International objection and reciprocity requirements still matter.

lessons.title: Repeater rules and the below-30-MHz exception
lessons.teachingSummary: A repeater automatically receives and retransmits another station's signal, usually on a separate input/output frequency. It increases useful coverage; it does not give the user the installer's qualifications or unrestricted access to new bands.

An unmodulated carrier below 30 MHz is permitted for brief tests. Keep it brief, identify as required and avoid interference. Repeatedly sending an empty carrier is not a substitute for proper on-air procedure.

lessons.title: Using a repeater courteously
lessons.teachingSummary: Listen first. To call a known station, say its call sign and then your own. To join a conversation, give your call sign during a pause. Leave pauses so others, especially a station with an emergency, can enter. Keep transmissions short; a repeater's time-out timer interrupts excessive continuous transmissions.
lessons.teaching:
Listen first. To call a known station, say its call sign and then your own. To join a conversation, give your call sign during a pause. Leave pauses so others, especially a station with an emergency, can enter. Keep transmissions short; a repeater's time-out timer interrupts excessive continuous transmissions.

Repeaters extend portable/mobile range by receiving at a favourable location and retransmitting. Frequency coordination recommends compatible repeater frequencies to reduce mutual interference. The common 2-metre offset is 600 kHz, but check the actual repeater's setting and direction.

CTCSS is a low-frequency, usually sub-audible access/squelch tone. A matching tone lets the receiver pass audio; it does not encrypt a conversation. Ask where are you in ordinary voice conversation rather than forcing a Q code into every sentence.

Example: if the repeater output is 146.940 MHz with a minus 600-kHz offset, you listen on 146.940 MHz and transmit on 146.340 MHz. A correct output frequency with an incorrect offset or access tone can prevent successful access.

lessons.title: CQ, direct calls, simplex and sidebands
lessons.teachingSummary: CQ is a general invitation for any station to answer. For the exam's voice format, say CQ three times, this is, then your call sign three times. To answer, give the other station's call sign once, this is, then your own. A direct call to a specific station similarly puts the called call sign first.

To answer, give the other station's call sign once, this is, then your own. A direct call to a specific station similarly puts the called call sign first.

Simplex means both stations transmit and receive on the same frequency. Use it when the direct path is reliable so the repeater remains available to others. Listening for the other station on the repeater input tests whether direct communication may work. Choose a simplex frequency that is not a local repeater input/output; consult the band plan.

VHF/UHF are generally preferred for local communication, keeping HF less congested for longer paths. For ordinary SSB voice convention, 20 metres uses USB; the bank's 3755-kHz example uses LSB. Convention does not eliminate the need to satisfy legal bandwidth and band-edge limits.

lessons.title: Listen, choose a frequency and test without interference
lessons.teachingSummary: Listen carefully before transmitting, then check whether the frequency is in use. No net or regular user owns a frequency. A net finding its normal channel occupied should politely ask about a move or choose a clear frequency; moving courteously can also help a net begin without conflict.
lessons.teaching:
Listen carefully before transmitting, then check whether the frequency is in use. No net or regular user owns a frequency. A net finding its normal channel occupied should politely ask about a move or choose a clear frequency; moving courteously can also help a net begin without conflict.

Use the minimum needed power. A dummy load absorbs RF for lengthy tests instead of radiating it. When antenna-tuner adjustment must be radiated near an ongoing HF SSB net, the bank recommends a clear frequency 3–5 kHz away, after checking that it is unused and legal.

Allow approximately 3 kHz separation from an SSB contact to avoid overlapping occupied bandwidth. If propagation changes bring rising interference, move to another clear frequency. A band plan is a voluntary division of a band among incompatible modes; it supports cooperation but is not the same as the legally binding allocation and bandwidth limits.

DEFrom
KAny station may reply

lessons.title: RS/RST reports and S-meter changes
lessons.teachingSummary: RS means readability and signal strength; RST adds tone for CW. Readability runs 1–5, signal strength 1–9, and tone 1–9. A 57 voice report is perfectly readable and moderately strong. A 33 is readable with considerable difficulty and weak. A 11 is unreadable and barely perceptible. In CW, 579 adds perfect tone; 459 is quite readable, fair strength and perfect tone.
lessons.teaching:
RS means readability and signal strength; RST adds tone for CW. Readability runs 1–5, signal strength 1–9, and tone 1–9. A 57 voice report is perfectly readable and moderately strong. A 33 is readable with considerable difficulty and weak. A 11 is unreadable and barely perceptible. In CW, 579 adds perfect tone; 459 is quite readable, fair strength and perfect tone.

An ideal calibrated S-meter changes 6 dB per S-unit, corresponding to a factor of four in power. Real meters vary, but use the stated standard when the question specifies it. S9 plus 20 dB is 20 dB stronger than S9, not twenty more S-units.

Worked example: if 100 W produces S9, reducing by 6 dB to 25 W produces S8 under unchanged propagation. Raising S8 to S9 requires four times the power. On a repeater, report the remote station's received audio/signal quality through the repeater rather than pretending your meter directly measures the remote transmitter's RF strength.

The S-meter shows S9 when receiving a station transmitting with 100 watts. Neglecting propagation changes, what transmitter power would cause your receiver's S-meter to read S8?

Correct answer: 25 watts

One calibrated S-unit is 6 dB, a fourfold power change. 100/4 = 25 W.

ISED B-002-006-008

Assume your receiver's S-meter is calibrated to a standard of 6 dB per S-unit per a recommendation by the International Amateur Radio Union (IARU). The S-meter on your receiver shows S8 when listening to a nearby transmitter. Approximately how much must the transmitter power be raised to increase the reading to S9?

Correct answer: 4 times

Raising one calibrated S-unit requires +6 dB, or approximately four times the transmitter power.

What does "RST 579" mean in a Morse code contact?

Correct answer: Your signal is perfectly readable, moderately strong, and with perfect tone

What does "RST 459" mean in a Morse code contact?

Correct answer: Your signal is quite readable, fair strength, and with perfect tone

ISED B-002-006-011

In voice contacts, what is the meaning of "Your signal report is 1 1"?

Correct answer: Your signal is unreadable, and barely perceptible

lessons.teachingSummary: Q codes are public procedural abbreviations. A question mark turns an appropriate statement into a question; context matters. On voice, ordinary words are often clearer, but learn the codes for CW and examination questions.
lessons.teaching:

CodeMeaning in these questions
QRSSend more slowly
QTHMy location is…
QRL?Is this frequency in use?
QSYChange frequency
QSBThe signal is fading
QRZ?Who is calling me?
QRMInterference from other signals
QRNStatic or natural noise
QRXI will call you again; wait

Example: before a CW CQ, send QRL? and listen for a response. Do not confuse QRM, QRN and QSB: interference, static and fading describe different causes of difficulty and may call for different remedies.

lessons.title: Distress priority and practical emergency readiness
lessons.teachingSummary: Use MAYDAY in voice or SOS in Morse for a life-threatening distress situation. The voice distress signal is MAYDAY repeated three times. Being stranded without immediate danger is urgent traffic, not automatically distress. Distress takes priority over the lower-priority emergency traffic described in the bank.
lessons.teaching:
Use MAYDAY in voice or SOS in Morse for a life-threatening distress situation. The voice distress signal is MAYDAY repeated three times. Being stranded without immediate danger is urgent traffic, not automatically distress. Distress takes priority over the lower-priority emergency traffic described in the bank.

To seek distress assistance through a busy repeater, break in during a pause, identify yourself and state the situation. If you hear a distress call, acknowledge it, establish the location and determine the assistance needed. If you cannot directly help, contact appropriate authorities and maintain a watch. Keep the channel available.

Prepare for loss of commercial AC power with charged batteries and a viable antenna. An adequate supply of charged handheld batteries matters more than optional accessories. A portable HF dipole or vertical can be deployed for emergency communication. Learn and practise deployment before it is needed; an emergency is a poor time to discover that connectors or power leads do not fit.

lessons.title: Logs, QSLs, maps, bearings and UTC
lessons.teachingSummary: A QSL card or compatible web log entry confirms that two amateur stations communicated. Keeping a station log is useful but is not a regulatory requirement in the bank's NOT-correct question. Record accurate call signs, dates, UTC times, bands and modes to support confirmations.
lessons.teaching:
A QSL card or compatible web log entry confirms that two amateur stations communicated. Keeping a station log is useful but is not a regulatory requirement in the bank's NOT-correct question. Record accurate call signs, dates, UTC times, bands and modes to support confirmations.

An azimuthal map centred on your location gives great-circle bearings to other places. The long path is opposite the short-path bearing: turn the antenna 180 degrees. For a short-path heading of 70 degrees, the long path is 250 degrees. A Maidenhead grid square expresses location as a four- or six-character code used in many VHF contacts and contests.

UTC is referenced to the Greenwich meridian. Convert using the stated offset, remembering date changes and daylight-saving differences. Worked example: local time at UTC−6 for a 19:00 UTC net is 19:00−6:00 = 13:00, or 1 PM. CHU, WWV and WWVH supply precise time/frequency reference signals; they are useful for checking equipment and schedules.

A directional antenna pointed in the long-path direction to another station is generally oriented how many degrees from its short-path heading?

Which statement about recording all contacts and unanswered CQ calls in a paper or computer-based station logbook is NOT correct?

lessons.title: Metric prefixes and reliable unit conversion
lessons.teachingSummary: Convert units before substituting numbers into a formula. Kilo (k) means 10³, mega (M) 10⁶ and giga (G) 10⁹. Milli (m) means 10⁻³, micro (µ) 10⁻⁶ and pico (p) 10⁻¹². Capitalization matters: mW and MW differ by a billion.

ConversionResult

If you have a hand-held transceiver that puts out 500 milliwatts, how many watts would this be?

A kilohm is:

How many megahertz is 7040 kHz?

Correct answer: 7.040 MHz

A current of one quarter ampere may be written as:

How many millivolts equal two volts?

lessons.title: Charge, current, voltage, resistance and conductance
lessons.teachingSummary: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge and is measured in amperes. Voltage, also called electromotive force or potential difference, drives current around a closed circuit. Resistance, R, opposes current and is measured in ohms. Conductance is the inverse: G = 1/R, measured in siemens.
lessons.teaching:
Current is the rate of flow of electric charge and is measured in amperes. Voltage, also called electromotive force or potential difference, drives current around a closed circuit. Resistance, R, opposes current and is measured in ohms. Conductance is the inverse: G = 1/R, measured in siemens.

Gold, silver, copper and aluminum are good conductors because their resistance is low. Glass, porcelain and air under ordinary conditions are good insulators. The question asking for the best conductor means the best among its particular answer choices; it does not mean copper outperforms silver in every comparison.

Polarity describes the positive/negative orientation in a DC circuit. A voltage drop develops as current passes through resistance: V = IR. Conductor resistance changes with temperature. A material's temperature coefficient determines the direction and rate; do not assume every material's resistance changes identically.

Worked example: 2 A through a 0.1-ohm wire path loses 0.2 V. Even a low resistance can cause a significant supply drop when current is large.

lessons.title: Power, continuity, open circuits and shorts
lessons.teachingSummary: Power is the rate of using or converting energy, measured in watts. For DC, P = VI: volts multiplied by amperes gives watts. A 100-W lamp uses energy faster than 40-, 50- or 60-W lamps. Energy over time is a different quantity: watt-hours = watts × hours.
lessons.teaching:
Power is the rate of using or converting energy, measured in watts. For DC, P = VI: volts multiplied by amperes gives watts. A 100-W lamp uses energy faster than 40-, 50- or 60-W lamps. Energy over time is a different quantity: watt-hours = watts × hours.

A closed circuit has continuity: an unbroken conducting path. An open circuit interrupts that path, so the ideal battery/resistor circuit draws no current. A short circuit creates an unintended very-low-resistance path, which can draw excessive current and blow a fuse immediately.

A burning resistor is dissipating more power as heat than its construction can safely remove. A fuse protects against overcurrent; never solve an immediately blowing fuse by simply fitting a larger one. First locate the short or other fault.

Worked example: a 12-V load drawing 2 A consumes 24 W. If a fault reduces circuit resistance to nearly zero, current can rise far beyond 2 A; the normal load rating does not limit the fault current.

Power is expressed in:

lessons.title: Ohm’s law with all three unknowns
lessons.teachingSummary: Ohm's law is V = IR. The bank sometimes writes E instead of V for voltage. Rearrange before calculating: I = V/R and R = V/I. Use volts, amperes and ohms; convert milliamperes into amperes first.

0.5 A through 2 ΩV = 0.5 × 21 V

ISED B-005-004-001

What is the voltage across a 2-ohm resistor if a current of 0.5 amperes flows through it?

Correct answer: 1.0 volts

Use V = IR: 0.5 A × 2 Ω = 1.0 V.

ISED B-005-004-002

How is the current in a DC circuit calculated when the voltage and resistance are known?

Correct answer: Current equals voltage divided by resistance

ISED B-005-004-003

How is the resistance in a DC circuit calculated when the voltage and current are known?

Correct answer: Resistance equals voltage divided by current

ISED B-005-004-004

How is the voltage in a DC circuit calculated when the current and resistance are known?

Correct answer: Voltage equals current multiplied by resistance

ISED B-005-004-005

What is the resistance of a circuit that draws 0.25 amperes from a 12-volt source?

Correct answer: 48 ohms

Use R = V/I: 12 V / 0.25 A = 48 Ω.

ISED B-005-004-006

What value of resistance is required to drop 9 volts with a current of 10 milliamperes?

Correct answer: 900 ohms

First convert 10 mA to 0.010 A. R = 9/0.010 = 900 Ω.

ISED B-005-004-007

If the current flowing through a 50-ohm resistor is 0.44 amperes, what voltage would you measure across the resistor?

Correct answer: 22 volts

Use V = IR: 0.44 × 50 = 22 V.

ISED B-005-004-008

A 30-ohm resistor is connected across a 6-volt battery. What current does it draw?

Correct answer: 0.2 amperes

Use I = V/R: 6/30 = 0.2 A.

ISED B-005-004-009

What voltage is needed to supply a current of 200 milliamperes to operate a relay that has a resistance of 25 ohms?

Correct answer: 5 volts

Convert 200 mA to 0.200 A, then V = IR = 0.200 × 25 = 5 V.

ISED B-005-004-010

What formula calculates the resistance of a circuit when the voltage and current are known?

Correct answer: R = E / I

ISED B-005-004-011

What is the resistance of a circuit if it draws 300 milliamperes from a 3-volt battery?

Correct answer: 10 ohms

Convert 300 mA to 0.300 A, then R = V/I = 3/0.300 = 10 Ω.

lessons.title: Series and parallel resistor circuits
lessons.teachingSummary: In series, every resistor carries the same current and the resistances add: Rtotal = R1 + R2 + …. Thus five 10-ohm resistors make 50 ohms, and five 24-ohm resistors make 120 ohms. Total series resistance exceeds any individual positive resistor.
lessons.teaching:
In series, every resistor carries the same current and the resistances add: Rtotal = R1 + R2 + …. Thus five 10-ohm resistors make 50 ohms, and five 24-ohm resistors make 120 ohms. Total series resistance exceeds any individual positive resistor.

In parallel, each branch has the same voltage and branch currents add. Use 1/Rtotal = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + …. For n equal resistors of value R, Rtotal = R/n. Parallel resistance is below the smallest individual positive resistance. A branch drawing twice the current at the same voltage has half the resistance.

Worked examples: four 100-ohm parallel branches each draw 12/100 = 0.12 A at 12 V; total is 4 × 0.12 = 0.48 A, or 480 mA. Two 1000-ohm resistors at 12 V each draw 12 mA, so total is 24 mA. Four 68-ohm resistors in parallel make 68/4 = 17 ohms.

Avoid adding parallel resistances directly. The extra paths reduce the equivalent resistance, even though the number of components increases.

ISED B-005-005-001

In a parallel circuit with a voltage source and several branch resistors, how is the total current related to the current in the branch resistors?

Correct answer: It equals the sum of the branch current through each resistor

ISED B-005-005-002

You connect four 100-ohm resistors in parallel across a 12-volt battery. How many milliamperes of current are drawn from the battery?

Correct answer: 480 mA

Each 100-Ω branch draws 12/100 = 0.12 A. Four parallel branches draw 4 × 0.12 = 0.48 A = 480 mA.

ISED B-005-005-003

Several resistors of various values are connected in parallel. How does the total resistance of the combination compare to the individual resistors?

Correct answer: It is less than the smallest resistor

ISED B-005-005-004

Two 1000-ohm resistors are connected in parallel across a 12-volt battery. What is the total current?

Correct answer: 24 milliamperes

Each 1000-Ω branch draws 12/1000 = 0.012 A. Two branches draw 0.024 A = 24 mA.

ISED B-005-005-005

The total resistance of resistors connected in series is:

Correct answer: greater than the resistance of any one resistor

ISED B-005-005-006

What is the total resistance of five 10-ohm resistors in series?

Correct answer: 50 ohms

Series resistances add: five × 10 Ω = 50 Ω.

ISED B-005-005-007

Which of these series combination of resistors would replace a single 120-ohm resistor?

Correct answer: Five 24-ohm resistors

Five equal 24-Ω resistors in series give 5 × 24 = 120 Ω.

ISED B-005-005-008

If ten resistors of equal value "R" are wired in parallel, what formula yields the total resistance?

Correct answer: R / 10

ISED B-005-005-009

What is the total resistance of four 68-ohm resistors wired in parallel?

Correct answer: 17 ohms

For four equal parallel resistors, divide one resistance by four: 68/4 = 17 Ω.

ISED B-005-005-010

Two resistors are in parallel. Resistor "A" carries twice the current of resistor "B," which means that:

Correct answer: "A" has half the resistance of "B"

Parallel branches have the same voltage. I = V/R means twice the current requires half the resistance.

ISED B-005-005-011

The total current in a parallel circuit is equal to the:

Correct answer: sum of the currents through all the parallel branches

lessons.title: Resistor heating and load power calculations
lessons.teachingSummary: For a resistive DC load use P = VI = I²R = V²/R. A physically larger resistor of the same resistance can normally dissipate more heat; wattage rating is not another way of stating resistance. At a fixed resistance, doubling voltage makes four times the power because voltage is squared.
lessons.teaching:
For a resistive DC load use P = VI = I²R = V²/R. A physically larger resistor of the same resistance can normally dissipate more heat; wattage rating is not another way of stating resistance. At a fixed resistance, doubling voltage makes four times the power because voltage is squared.

Two equal 1-W resistors can together dissipate 2 W when each shares the heat equally, in series or parallel. Two 100-ohm resistors in parallel replace 50 ohms while doubling the available power rating. Four 200-ohm, 2-W resistors in parallel make 50 ohms with 8 W of total rating, enough for a 5-W dummy load under the stated ideal sharing conditions.

Worked examples: 12 V × 5 A = 60 W minimum ideal transformer output; 12 V × 0.500 A = 6 W DC input; a 30-W lamp at 12 V takes 30/12 = 2.5 A. Two 10-ohm resistors in series at 10 V make 20 ohms: P = 10²/20 = 5 W total, 2.5 W in each equal resistor.

Practical designs need thermal margin, ventilation and appropriate RF construction; a calculated DC wattage alone does not prove a home-built load behaves well at RF.

ISED B-005-006-001

Why would a large size resistor be used instead of a smaller one of the same resistance?

Correct answer: For greater power dissipation

ISED B-005-006-002

A load requires 12 volts DC at 5 amperes. What is the minimum required power transformer rating?

Correct answer: 60 watts

The ideal minimum output power is V × I = 12 × 5 = 60 W. Real supply designs need additional margin.

ISED B-005-006-003

What is the DC input power of a transmitter operating at 12 volts and drawing 500 milliamperes?

Correct answer: 6 watts

500 mA = 0.5 A. DC input power is 12 × 0.5 = 6 W.

ISED B-005-006-004

When two 500-ohm 1-watt resistors are connected in series, the maximum total power that can be dissipated by the resistors is:

Correct answer: 2 watts

The two equal series resistors share the heat equally. Each may dissipate 1 W, for 2 W total.

ISED B-005-006-005

When two 500-ohm 1-watt resistors are connected in parallel, they can dissipate a maximum total power of:

Correct answer: 2 watts

The equal parallel resistors share the power equally. Two 1-W ratings allow 2 W total under the stated conditions.

ISED B-005-006-006

If the voltage applied to two resistors in series is doubled, how much will the total power change?

Correct answer: Increase four times

At unchanged resistance, P = V²/R. Doubling voltage multiplies power by 2² = 4.

ISED B-005-006-007

Which of these combinations of resistors could make up a 50-ohm dummy load capable of safely dissipating 5 watts?

Correct answer: Four 2-watt 200-ohm resistors in parallel

Four equal 200-Ω parallel resistors make 200/4 = 50 Ω. Their 2-W ratings total 8 W, exceeding the required 5 W.

ISED B-005-006-008

How much current is drawn by a 12-volt, 30-watt light bulb?

Correct answer: 2.5 amperes

Rearrange P = VI into I = P/V: 30/12 = 2.5 A.

ISED B-005-006-009

What is the power consumption of two 10-ohm resistors connected in series with a 10-volt battery?

Correct answer: 5 watts

The series resistance is 10 + 10 = 20 Ω. P = V²/R = 100/20 = 5 W total.

ISED B-005-006-010

What is the advantage of replacing a 50-ohm resistor with a parallel combination of two 100-ohm resistors of the same power rating?

Correct answer: Same resistance but greater power rating

ISED B-005-006-011

Resistor wattage ratings are:

Correct answer: determined by heat dissipation qualities

lessons.title: AC cycles, phase, frequency and wavelength
lessons.teachingSummary: Frequency counts complete cycles per second, in hertz. A 60-Hz sine wave completes 60 cycles each second. Household AC is nominally sinusoidal; DC has a fixed polarity. Two same-frequency waves whose cycles occur at different times have a phase difference.
lessons.teaching:
Frequency counts complete cycles per second, in hertz. A 60-Hz sine wave completes 60 cycles each second. Household AC is nominally sinusoidal; DC has a fixed polarity. Two same-frequency waves whose cycles occur at different times have a phase difference.

The approximate human audio range is 20 Hz–20 kHz. Amateur speech equipment commonly uses a narrower portion. HF is 3–30 MHz, so 7125 kHz = 7.125 MHz is HF. A harmonic is an integer multiple of a fundamental: 4 kHz is the second harmonic of 2 kHz.

Wavelength is the distance a wave travels during one complete cycle. In free space, λ = c/f, approximately λ(m) = 300/f(MHz). Increasing frequency reduces wavelength; decreasing wavelength implies increasing frequency. Period is the time per cycle, T = 1/f. At 1 kHz, T = 1 ms. Do not confuse a distance (wavelength) with a time (period).

lessons.title: Decibels, power ratios and signal reports
lessons.teachingSummary: A decibel expresses a ratio. For power, dB = 10 log10(Pout/Pin). Positive dB is gain; negative dB is loss. Memorize power steps: +3 dB is approximately ×2, +6 dB ×4, +9 dB ×8, +10 dB ×10. For a loss, divide by the same factor. Add dB values for cascaded gain/loss; do not add the linear power ratios.
lessons.teaching:
A decibel expresses a ratio. For power, dB = 10 log10(Pout/Pin). Positive dB is gain; negative dB is loss. Memorize power steps: +3 dB is approximately ×2, +6 dB ×4, +9 dB ×8, +10 dB ×10. For a loss, divide by the same factor. Add dB values for cascaded gain/loss; do not add the linear power ratios.

Worked examples: 2 W with 9 dB gain becomes about 16 W. A 100-W signal with 6 dB line loss delivers about 25 W to the antenna. Increasing 5 W to 50 W is a ×10 ratio, or +10 dB.

For a calibrated report, reducing 200 W to 20 W removes 10 dB: S9+10 dB becomes S9. Reducing 150 W to 15 W changes S9+20 dB into S9+10 dB. Removing 30 dB from 100 W divides by 1000 and leaves 0.1 W. These examples assume unchanged paths and a properly calibrated receiver; actual S-meters and propagation vary.

ISED B-005-008-001

A two-times increase in power results in a change of how many dB?

Correct answer: 3 dB higher

ISED B-005-008-002

What change in transmitter power results in a 3 dB decrease?

Correct answer: Divide the original power by 2

ISED B-005-008-003

What change in transmitter power results in a 6 dB increase?

Correct answer: Multiply the original power by 4

ISED B-005-008-004

If a signal transmitted with a power of 200 watts is received with an S-meter reading of "10 dB over S9," what would be the new reading if power was reduced to 20 watts?

Correct answer: S9

200 W to 20 W is a tenfold reduction, or −10 dB. Subtract 10 dB from S9+10 dB to obtain S9.

ISED B-005-008-005

If a signal transmitted with a power of 150 watts is received with an S-meter reading of "20 dB over S9," what would be the new reading if power was reduced to 15 watts?

Correct answer: S9 plus 10 dB

150 W to 15 W removes 10 dB. S9+20 dB therefore becomes S9+10 dB.

ISED B-005-008-006

What is the "decibel" used for?

Correct answer: To measure the ratio of two signals

ISED B-005-008-007

The power output from a transmitter increases from 1 watt to 2 watts. How many decibels does that increase represent?

Correct answer: 3 dB

ISED B-005-008-008

The power of a transmitter is increased from 5 watts to 50 watts by a linear amplifier. The power gain, expressed in dB, is:

Correct answer: 10 dB

50/5 = 10 times the power. 10 log10(10) = 10 dB.

ISED B-005-008-009

You add a 9 dB gain amplifier to your 2-watt hand-held. What is the power output of the combination?

Correct answer: 16 watts

9 dB is approximately three 3-dB doublings: 2 W × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16 W.

ISED B-005-008-010

The power of your transmitter is 100 watts and your transmission line introduces a loss of 6 dB. How much power is delivered to the antenna?

Correct answer: 25 watts

6 dB loss is approximately division by four. 100/4 = 25 W.

ISED B-005-008-011

A local amateur radio operator reports receiving your 100-watt 2-metre simplex transmission with an S-meter reading of "30 dB over S9." What power could you use to reduce that reading to S9?

Correct answer: 0.1 W

A 30-dB reduction divides power by 1000: 100 W / 1000 = 0.1 W.

lessons.title: Measuring voltage, current, resistance and RF power
lessons.teachingSummary: A voltmeter measures potential difference across a component, so connect it in parallel. Its high input resistance limits the current it draws from the circuit. An ammeter measures the current through a path, so insert it in series. Its very low resistance minimizes the added voltage drop.
lessons.teaching:
A voltmeter measures potential difference across a component, so connect it in parallel. Its high input resistance limits the current it draws from the circuit. An ammeter measures the current through a path, so insert it in series. Its very low resistance minimizes the added voltage drop.

A multimeter commonly measures voltage, current and resistance. Use a resistance range only on a de-energized circuit after safely removing stored energy; the meter supplies its own small test source. The proper instrument for final-amplifier DC current is an ammeter. For direct transmitter RF output-power measurement use an RF wattmeter and a suitable load/line arrangement, rather than assuming DC input equals RF output.

Accuracy means closeness to the true value, not how many digits the display has. Check the correct input jack, range and rating before connecting probes. In particular, placing an ammeter directly across a supply creates a short through the meter, which can damage it or cause injury.

lessons.title: Amplifier gain, efficiency and feedback
lessons.teachingSummary: An amplifier increases a signal's voltage, current or power by drawing energy from a supply. An RF amplifier handles radio-frequency signals; an audio amplifier handles microphone or speaker signals. A speech amplifier commonly processes roughly 300–3000 Hz, a narrower band than full human hearing.
lessons.teaching:
An amplifier increases a signal's voltage, current or power by drawing energy from a supply. An RF amplifier handles radio-frequency signals; an audio amplifier handles microphone or speaker signals. A speech amplifier commonly processes roughly 300–3000 Hz, a narrower band than full human hearing.

Gain is the increase or output-to-input ratio, often expressed in dB. A label such as gain = 10 dB suggests amplification. Efficiency instead compares useful output power with DC supply input: efficiency = RF output/DC input × 100%. Gain and efficiency do not describe the same ratio.

A linear amplifier preserves the waveform shape. Driving it into non-linear operation causes distortion and additional unwanted frequency components. Excessive positive feedback can make the amplifier oscillate instead of merely amplifying its input. Energy is supplied by the DC source; an amplifier does not create power without an energy input.

lessons.title: Diodes: direction, detection, regulation and light
lessons.teachingSummary: A semiconductor diode has an anode and cathode. In forward bias it conducts readily in one direction; reverse bias normally blocks current within its ratings. Conventional current flows anode to cathode; electron flow is cathode to anode. Questions about electrons therefore require the reverse direction from conventional-current diagrams.
lessons.teaching:
A semiconductor diode has an anode and cathode. In forward bias it conducts readily in one direction; reverse bias normally blocks current within its ratings. Conventional current flows anode to cathode; electron flow is cathode to anode. Questions about electrons therefore require the reverse direction from conventional-current diagrams.

A series diode in a radio's positive supply lead can block a reverse-polarity connection. Rectification converts alternating current to pulsating direct current; smoothing requires additional filtering. Detection recovers information from an RF signal. A Zener diode operates in its specified reverse-breakdown region to maintain or regulate voltage. An LED emits light, with colour determined by its semiconductor materials.

Worked distinction: a diode connected to AC does not produce perfectly smooth DC by itself. It passes one polarity of the waveform. A following filter capacitor reduces the resulting ripple; a regulator can then stabilize the voltage.

lessons.title: Bipolar transistors as amplifiers and switches
lessons.teachingSummary: A bipolar junction transistor has collector, base and emitter electrodes. A small change at the base controls a larger collector/emitter current, allowing a low-level signal to be amplified with relatively low supply voltages. The base also controls the state when the device is used as a switch.
lessons.teaching:
A bipolar junction transistor has collector, base and emitter electrodes. A small change at the base controls a larger collector/emitter current, allowing a low-level signal to be amplified with relatively low supply voltages. The base also controls the state when the device is used as a switch.

NPN and PNP are the two basic polarities. Their supply/bias polarities are reversed, so a PNP is not a direct replacement for an NPN in an unchanged circuit. A part described as a general-purpose audio NPN device is a bipolar transistor.

In cut-off the transistor is effectively off; in saturation it is strongly on. Alternating between those states makes a switch. lessons.title: Field-effect transistors and high input impedance
lessons.teachingSummary: A field-effect transistor has source, gate and drain. Charge carriers enter its channel at the source and leave at the drain. The gate controls channel conduction. N-channel and P-channel describe the two basic channel polarities.
lessons.teaching:
A field-effect transistor has source, gate and drain. Charge carriers enter its channel at the source and leave at the drain. The gate controls channel conduction. N-channel and P-channel describe the two basic channel polarities.

The gate needs very little steady current in the idealized high-impedance model used by these questions. In a reverse-biased junction FET, decreasing the reverse gate bias allows more channel current. That particular rule describes the depletion/JFET context, not a universal statement for every MOSFET operating mode. Real devices have leakage and capacitance; the bank's phrase gate never conducts current is an idealization.

For functional comparisons, the bipolar transistor's emitter corresponds to a FET's source, collector to drain, and base is the controlling terminal analogous to the gate. Source and drain connect to the ends of the channel. High input impedance means the controlling input does not heavily load the preceding circuit.

lessons.title: Vacuum triodes and their transistor analogies
lessons.teachingSummary: A triode contains a cathode, one control grid and a plate (anode) inside an evacuated envelope. The cathode emits electrons, the positively biased plate collects them, and the grid controls the flow. Output current flows between cathode and plate; the plate normally has the highest positive operating voltage.

Output current flows between cathode and plate; the plate normally has the highest positive operating voltage.

Both triodes and transistors can amplify. A field-effect transistor is the closest analogy among the semiconductor choices because a control voltage at the gate/grid regulates current with high input impedance. A tube may be selected for a high-power application, but it also requires heating and can involve dangerous supply voltages and stored energy.

lessons.title: Resistor colour codes, tolerance and temperature
lessons.teachingSummary: A four-band resistor uses two significant digits, a power-of-ten multiplier and a tolerance band. The first three bands give resistance in ohms; the fourth gives percentage tolerance. Changing 33 Ω to 39 Ω changes the second digit band. Changing 120 Ω to 1200 Ω changes the multiplier, or third band.
lessons.teaching:
A four-band resistor uses two significant digits, a power-of-ten multiplier and a tolerance band. The first three bands give resistance in ohms; the fourth gives percentage tolerance. Changing 33 Ω to 39 Ω changes the second digit band. Changing 120 Ω to 1200 Ω changes the multiplier, or third band.

DigitColourDigitColour
0Black5Green
1Brown6Blue
2Red7Violet
3Orange8Grey
4Yellow9White

Worked code: red, violet, yellow means 27 × 10⁴ = 270,000 Ω = 270 kΩ. A 100-ohm resistor with ±10% tolerance can be 90–110 ohms. A smaller tolerance percentage is more precise: 0.1% is tighter than 20%. Gold commonly denotes ±5%, silver ±10%, and no band ±20%.

Temperature coefficient specifies fractional resistance change per degree Celsius, often in ppm/°C. Its sign and magnitude determine how resistance changes as temperature rises; tolerance and temperature coefficient are different ratings.

lessons.title: Combining inductors and capacitors
lessons.teachingSummary: An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field; a capacitor stores energy in an electric field between separated conductors. Coil diameter, length and number of turns determine an air-core coil's inductance. Capacitor plate area and spacing affect capacitance: larger area increases it and larger separation decreases it, with the dielectric also important.
lessons.teaching:
An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field; a capacitor stores energy in an electric field between separated conductors. Coil diameter, length and number of turns determine an air-core coil's inductance. Capacitor plate area and spacing affect capacitance: larger area increases it and larger separation decreases it, with the dielectric also important.

Uncoupled inductors combine like resistors: series values add, while parallel values combine reciprocally. Two equal series inductors give twice one value; two equal parallel inductors give half. Capacitors use the opposite pattern: parallel capacitances add and series capacitances combine reciprocally.

Worked examples: two 12-mH series chokes make 24 mH; two 20-mH parallel coils make 10 mH. Two 20-µF series capacitors make 10 µF; two 24-µF parallel capacitors make 48 µF. These simple coil rules assume negligible mutual magnetic coupling.

Polarized electrolytic capacitors must not have reverse voltage applied. Observe voltage ratings as well as polarity; disconnecting a supply does not guarantee that a capacitor has discharged.

lessons.title: Reactance, impedance, RF chokes and bypasses
lessons.teachingSummary: Reactance is frequency-dependent opposition to AC. For an inductor, XL = 2πfL, so inductive reactance increases with frequency. For a capacitor, XC = 1/(2πfC), so capacitive reactance decreases with frequency. Use hertz, henries and farads in these formulas. Impedance combines resistance and reactance and is the AC voltage/current ratio.
lessons.teaching:
Reactance is frequency-dependent opposition to AC. For an inductor, XL = 2πfL, so inductive reactance increases with frequency. For a capacitor, XC = 1/(2πfC), so capacitive reactance decreases with frequency. Use hertz, henries and farads in these formulas. Impedance combines resistance and reactance and is the AC voltage/current ratio.

An RF choke passes DC or low-frequency signals relatively easily but presents high impedance to unwanted RF. Winding a cable on ferrite can raise its common-mode impedance at radio frequencies. A small bypass capacitor does the complementary job: it provides a low-reactance path for RF while having higher reactance at audio frequencies.

Worked comparison: doubling frequency doubles XL but halves XC. A component chosen to block RF need not block audio, and a capacitor chosen to shunt RF need not short out the desired speech signal. Real ferrites and capacitors have losses and frequency limits, so this model explains the principle rather than every real component at every frequency.

lessons.title: Induction and transformer ratios
lessons.teachingSummary: Current creates a magnetic field; in air, field strength around a conductor is proportional to current. Changing magnetic flux induces voltage. The largest induced voltage occurs at the greatest rate of change, not necessarily the greatest instantaneous current. Nearby parallel wires couple more strongly; steel is a suitable permanent-magnet material.
lessons.teaching:
Current creates a magnetic field; in air, field strength around a conductor is proportional to current. Changing magnetic flux induces voltage. The largest induced voltage occurs at the greatest rate of change, not necessarily the greatest instantaneous current. Nearby parallel wires couple more strongly; steel is a suitable permanent-magnet material.

An ideal transformer's voltage ratio equals its turns ratio: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Current changes inversely so input power equals output power when losses are ignored: VpIp = VsIs. Impedance transforms by the square of the turns ratio. Actual core and copper losses produce heat, including warm iron laminations.

Worked examples: 250 turns to 500 turns steps 120 V up to 240 V. A 120-V primary drawing 0.5 A supplies 60 W, so a 12-V secondary supplies 5 A. A 250-W load at 120 V draws 250/120 ≈ 2.1 A. A 10-W, 5-V secondary supplies 2 A. With a 1:5 step-up ratio, 50 mA secondary current requires 250 mA primary current.

lessons.title: Series and parallel resonance
lessons.teachingSummary: An inductor and capacitor form a tuned circuit. At resonance their reactances have equal magnitudes and opposite signs: XL = XC. The ideal frequency is f = 1/(2π√LC). Increasing L or C lowers this frequency; reducing either raises it.
lessons.teaching:
An inductor and capacitor form a tuned circuit. At resonance their reactances have equal magnitudes and opposite signs: XL = XC. The ideal frequency is f = 1/(2π√LC). Increasing L or C lowers this frequency; reducing either raises it.

A series-resonant circuit has minimum impedance and maximum current at resonance, limited by its resistance. A parallel-resonant circuit has high input impedance at resonance. Do not swap the series and parallel answers. These effects let tuned circuits select desired receiver frequencies and implement filters.

Bandwidth is the range around resonance over which the circuit has its useful response. In the simplified exam model, adding resistance does not change the L/C-defined resonant frequency, but it does affect damping, response and bandwidth. Real circuit peak frequencies can shift with losses and loading.

Worked example: 10 µH and 100 pF give about 5.03 MHz. Doubling both components makes their product four times larger, so frequency halves to about 2.52 MHz. Try these relationships in the LC resonance lab, then compare them with the antenna lab's matching network.

lessons.title: CW, AM, frequency stability and waste heat
lessons.teachingSummary: CW Morse is an interrupted RF carrier. Chirp is a small unwanted frequency change as each dit or dah begins/ends, often due to supply voltage varying with keying load. A steady supply and a mechanically/electrically stable oscillator prevent unwanted chirp and drift. A VFO allows tuning beyond the set of frequencies supplied by individual crystals.
lessons.teaching:
CW Morse is an interrupted RF carrier. Chirp is a small unwanted frequency change as each dit or dah begins/ends, often due to supply voltage varying with keying load. A steady supply and a mechanically/electrically stable oscillator prevent unwanted chirp and drift. A VFO allows tuning beyond the set of frequencies supplied by individual crystals.

AM varies the RF envelope amplitude with the modulating audio. Conventional AM contains a carrier and both sidebands. Its occupied bandwidth is approximately twice the highest modulating-audio frequency. Thus speech extending to 3 kHz produces about 6 kHz total AM bandwidth.

An amplifier converts only part of its DC input into useful RF output. The rest becomes heat. Worked example: with 200 W DC input and 125 W RF output, 200−125 = 75 W is dissipated as heat, and efficiency is 125/200 × 100% = 62.5%. Do not confuse DC input, RF output, gain and efficiency.

ISED B-003-011-001

What does chirp mean?

Correct answer: A small change in the output frequency of a transmitter each time a dit or dah is sent

ISED B-003-011-002

What can be done to keep a CW transmitter from chirping?

Correct answer: Keep the power supply voltages very steady under varying loads

ISED B-003-011-003

What is the advantage of using a variable frequency oscillator in a basic CW transmitter?

Correct answer: Frequency is not constrained to the available crystals

ISED B-003-011-004

Which type of transmitter modulation changes the amplitude of an RF wave for the purpose of conveying information?

Correct answer: Amplitude modulation

ISED B-003-011-005

In what emission mode does the instantaneous amplitude (envelope) of the RF signal vary with the modulating audio?

Correct answer: Amplitude modulation

ISED B-003-011-006

Morse code is usually transmitted by radio as:

Correct answer: an interrupted carrier

You are transmitting using amplitude modulation. What bandwidth does your signal occupy if the highest frequency of your voice is 3 kHz?

Correct answer: 6 kHz

Conventional AM occupies both sidebands, so bandwidth is twice the highest audio frequency: 2 × 3 kHz = 6 kHz.

Correct answer: Carrier and two sidebands
